welcome.script:
Welcome back to the Field Station, scientists!

[ON SCREEN: The hawk]
Remember our hawk at post 7?

[ON SCREEN: The missing frogs]
After a long dry spell, the green tree frogs left the marsh. At night, it went silent. (Cup your hand to your ear.) Not one frog calling.

[ON SCREEN: The volunteer’s note]
A volunteer left this note: “The hawk will starve, and nothing else will change.” Hmm. Is she right?

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
That’s our case. Find four clues, then crack it. Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · more or fewer? (Clue 1)

parts.label: ⬆️⬇️ Sort the cards
parts.title: More or fewer?
rows: Drag the card to More or Fewer.

warmup.script:
(Stack three books or blocks in a tower.) Watch. What happens if I pull out the middle one?

[ON SCREEN: A food chain]
A food chain is a little like this tower. Grass, rabbits, foxes. Now the rabbits disappear. Does the grass get more, or fewer? And the foxes?

[ON SCREEN: Sort the cards]
Sort all six cards. Then write your reasons. Press Listen. Dr. Reyes has a tip.

part2.label: Part 2 · the hawk photo (Clue 2)
part2.script:
(Hold up a plate.) If your only food were pizza, and the pizza ran out, you’d be in trouble! But you eat lots of foods.

[ON SCREEN: The hawk photo]
Look what this real hawk caught in the Everglades. That’s not a frog! Tap every number on the photo.

[ON SCREEN: A food web]
When animals eat many things, their food chains connect into a food web.

Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

part3.label: Part 3 · the missing-link test (Clue 3)

parts.label: 🔓 To unlock
parts.title: Frogs AND hawks
parts.body: Run the frog test and the hawk test. Then answer the question.

part3.script:
[ON SCREEN: The model]
Scientists can’t take every frog out of a real marsh just to see what happens. So we use a model.

Pick one living thing to remove. Predict: will the others have more, fewer, or about the same? Then press Run and watch four seasons go by.

[ON SCREEN: Grasshoppers]
Keep an eye on the grasshoppers.

[ON SCREEN: To unlock]
Test the frogs AND the hawks. Some bars might surprise you! Press Listen first.

explore.label: Part 4 · test the volunteer’s note (Clue 4)

parts.label: ✅❌ Stamp it
parts.title: Supported or not?
rows: Pick the line that proves it.

explore.script:
[ON SCREEN: Three predictions]
Time to check the volunteer’s note. She made three predictions.

[ON SCREEN: Stamp it]
(Pretend to stamp a paper on your desk.) Stamp each one. Supported means the evidence agrees. Not supported means it doesn’t. Then pick the line that proves it.

[ON SCREEN: The marsh]
Use your hawk photo and your missing-link test. Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
Four clues! At the top of this tab, crack the case: what really happens when the frogs leave?

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then write your case report: two short answers, your own Florida food chain with one link missing, and a CER. Remember the frogs in the hawk test? Did they grow forever?

[ON SCREEN: Help buttons]
Stuck? Press Hint. Your answers save as you type. Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🐛 Your specimen
parts.title: Caterpillar
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Coming up
parts.title: A giant oak falls
parts.body: A storm knocks down one big tree. What changes in the forest?

closing.script:
Case closed! The hawk switched to snakes and mice. But the marsh still changed: more grasshoppers, less sawgrass. One missing link ripples both ways!

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist to add a caterpillar to your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Coming up]
Coming up: a giant oak falls in a storm. What happens to the forest around it?

Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s last word.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The quote
parts.title: Some people say…
parts.body: “If a top predator like a hawk disappears, the prey will just keep growing forever, and the ecosystem will be fine.”

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The quote]
Some people say that if the hawk disappears, the prey grows forever. Hmm. Look back at your hawk test. Tap your side in the planner, pick two pieces of evidence, then write your reasoning. Try starting with “This shows that…”

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.

vr.script:
Hi, scientists! Remember the volunteer’s note? (Hold up a sticky note.) “No frogs? Then the hawk will starve.”

[ON SCREEN: The note]
Today you’ll find out if she’s right. You won’t build anything. You’ll do a field survey: a careful look at every living thing in one place.

[ON SCREEN: Two ways]
Pick your way at the top. With a headset, walk the Everglades in VR. No headset? Take the boardwalk photo walk.

[ON SCREEN: Field notes]
Either way, write down at least five living things in your field notes, and ask: could a hawk eat this one?

[ON SCREEN: The badge]
Finish in VR and you earn the Red-Shoulder Feather badge!

Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.
